title: Applied ML: quantization & eval scratchpad (2026-03-21)
content:
2026-03-21 — quick scratchpad for quantization + eval runs

Goal:
- Get a quick read on quality vs perf for Llama-2-13B (hf checkpoint) under our q4_0 and q8_0 quantization profiles. Baseline is fp16.
- Collect latency/throughput numbers on a single A10x8 (dev box) and memory usage to guide Dedicated configs.
- Short eval on a ~100-example QA prompt set (mix of short/long). Not a final benchmark, just directional.

Setup:
- Model: llama-2-13b (hf id: meta/llama-2-13b) converted with our export pipeline.
- Tokenizer: HF tokenizer (vocab unchanged). Max input length: 1024 tokens.
- Eval set: 100 QA samples (internal subset: sqaud-like short/long mix).
- Seed: 42. Batch size (inference): 1 (latency mode) and 8 (throughput/batch mode).
- Server: local docker image rw-inference:dev-20260321, GPU: A100-40GB in dev cluster.

Commands (notes):
- Export -> quantize -> serve (examples):
  ./scripts/export_model.sh --model meta/llama-2-13b --out /tmp/llama13b-fp16
  ./scripts/quantize.sh /tmp/llama13b-fp16 q4_0 /tmp/llama13b-q4_0
  ./scripts/quantize.sh /tmp/llama13b-fp16 q8_0 /tmp/llama13b-q8_0
  docker run --gpus all -v /tmp/models:/models rw-inference:dev-20260321 \\n    --model-path /models/llama13b-q4_0 --port 8080 --max-seq 1024

- Quick client inference (latency):
  curl -X POST localhost:8080/generate -d '{"prompt":"<PROMPT>","max_tokens":128,"temperature":0.0}'

Quant configs tested:
- baseline: fp16 (no quant)
- q8_0: 8-bit per-tensor scheme (our stable q8 variant)
- q4_0: 4-bit groupwise (fastest, smallest memory)

Eval prompt template (QA):
- system: "You are a helpful assistant. Answer concisely."
- user: "Q: <context> \nQuestion: <question>\nAnswer:"

Examples used in run (representative):
1) context: "The Wright brothers flew the first controlled airplane in 1903." question: "When did the Wright brothers first fly?"
2) long context (600 tokens) about Keynesian economics; question: "What is the basic idea behind fiscal stimulus?"

Results (summary - single-run, directional):
- FP16 baseline (batch=1):
  - avg latency (wall per-token): 1.9 ms/token (stdev 0.3)
  - throughput: ~5200 tokens/s
  - GPU mem: ~27.5 GB (model + KV cache typical)
  - QA EM: 72.4%

- q8_0 (batch=1):
  - avg latency: 1.45 ms/token (stdev 0.25)
  - throughput: ~6800 tokens/s
  - GPU mem: ~18.3 GB
  - QA EM: 71.9% (delta -0.5 pts)

- q4_0 (batch=1):
  - avg latency: 1.15 ms/token (stdev 0.2)
  - throughput: ~8600 tokens/s
  - GPU mem: ~11.1 GB
  - QA EM: 69.1% (delta -3.3 pts vs fp16)

Batch mode (batch=8) — focus on throughput (observed peak tokens/s):
- FP16: ~39k tokens/s
- q8_0: ~52k tokens/s
- q4_0: ~68k tokens/s

Observations / notes:
- q8_0 gives a nice perf uplift with minimal quality loss on this small QA set (0.5 pt EM). Good candidate for Dedicated baseline if we want lower memory with near-baseline quality.
- q4_0 is tempting for cost/throughput but has noticeable quality drop on longer-context items and when reasoning is required. More investigation needed on where the degradation occurs (tokens near the end? specific token distributions?).
- Memory savings for q4_0 are large; would enable packing more replicas per GPU or smaller GPUs for Dedicated.
- Decoder stability: q4_0 had 2/100 outputs with repeated loops (generation collapse) at temp=0.2 in one run. Need to re-check seed and beam settings. Might be mitigated by better groupwise scales (experiment with per-channel scaling).

Quick qualitative examples (cases where q4_0 failed vs fp16):
- Example 27 (long context, multi-step reasoning): fp16 gave a 3-step concise reasoning answer; q4_0 produced a shorter, partially incorrect reasoning chain (missed a premise).
- Example 61 (date extraction): fp16 -> "1903" ; q4_0 -> "around 1900s" (under-specific).

Immediate next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Re-run q4_0 with deterministic sampling (temp=0.0) and compare (to rule out sampler noise).
- [ ] Run targeted ablation on long-context subset (n=30) to quantify EM drop vs context length.
- [ ] Try mixed precision hybrid: q4_0 for MLPs + fp16 for attention (if pipeline supports) — hypothesize quality recovery with small perf cost. Open GH PR to enable config. (see linked PR).
- [ ] Check generation collapse seeds; add guard in client to detect repetition and fallback to q8_0. Track telemetry (sample id + model variant).
- [ ] Cost calc: estimate tokens/s -> hourly throughput -> cost for Dedicated 1xA100. Rough draft: if q4_0 increases tokens/s by ~1.6x vs fp16, cost/unit dropping potential ~35-40% (very rough).

Issues / debugging notes:
- Observed one docker OOM when trying to run q8_0 on a 24GB dev GPU image (expected, but note for team: need minimum 32GB for q8_0 with 13B and 1k context in our build).
- Some eval runs hit HF tokenization warnings for long inputs (>1024); trimming logic works but need to log when we truncate examples.

Notes for product/platform:
- q8_0 looks like the low-risk quant variant to recommend as "recommended" for customers who want memory savings with minimal quality impact. q4_0 is "experimental/optimize for cost" — should be flagged in console as "quality may degrade for long-context or reasoning tasks".
- Suggest an initial rollout: enable q8_0 as an option in Redwood Console for Llama-2-13B with a warning blurb; keep q4_0 behind an "advanced" toggle and require customers to opt-in.

Links to deeper runs / artifacts (local):
- /tmp/evals/2026-03-21/q4_0_run_01/results.csv
- /tmp/evals/2026-03-21/q8_0_run_01/results.csv
- /tmp/models/llama13b-q4_0/logs/debug-2026-03-21.txt

Open questions:
- How well do these deltas generalize to instruction-following tasks (chat) vs QA? Need a small chat eval next.
- Is the generation collapse reproducible across seeds/hardware?

Random notes to self:
- Jordan suggested checking group size parameter (gsize=64 vs 128) for q4. Try next run with gsize=128 (may improve quality at minor perf cost).
- Asha will run a separate eval on our long-context pipeline (up to 4096) using same quant profiles; watch for perf cliffs.

Bottom line (today):
- q8_0 = good tradeoff (recommended experiment stage).
- q4_0 = high reward for throughput/cost but quality risk; needs more focused tests and mitigations before recommending broadly.

-- maya
